newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds boosted by Treasuries, volumes tiny.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds boosted by Treasuries, volumes tiny.

text.p: Irish bonds edged higher on Monday, receiving a boost from recent gains by U.S. Treasuries and German Bunds, but trading volume was tiny, dealers said.
They said the market was expected to remain in hibernation until after Wednesday's New Year holiday.
Thursday's November credit-growth figures from the central bank and Friday's release of the goverment borrowing requirement for 1996 could prod the market back to life, dealers added.
"Volumes have been tiny and there is little to report," one dealer said. "We started reasonably well, thanks to gains in the U.S. and Germany, and little has happened since."
By 1550 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was 10p firmer at 101.70 to yield 5.99 percent, while the eight percent bond due 2006 was up 20p at 109.07, yielding 6.58 percent.
"It's certainly not going to get any busier ahead of the New Year," one dealer said. "Friday's Exchequer Borrowing Requirement (EBR) will be the next domestic focus."
